# Exact midpoint-compression comparison and obstruction

These statements concern fractional convex-hull packing, not halfspace
depth itself. They close the mass-preserving same-parity vertex-merging
route, including its adaptive version subject to choosing a same-parity
pair of current hull vertices.

## 1. A valid comparison, with its sharp loss

Let u,v be distinct source points, m=(u+v)/2, and let w be nonnegative
weights on a finite set containing u,v,m. Let 0<=delta<=min(w_u,w_v), and
put

    w'=w-delta e_u-delta e_v+2delta e_m.

For every target z, with the same available geometric source set,

    f_{w'}(z)<=f_w(z)+delta.                         (1)

Proof. Start with an optimal packing for w'. Split its groups, if needed,
so at most 2delta total group weight using m is assigned to the newly
added capacity there, and all remaining groups fit the capacities
w-delta e_u-delta e_v. Write t<=2delta for that selected group weight.
For each selected group A containing m, replace it by
(A without {m}) union {u,v}, using half its old packing weight. This
new group contains z in its convex hull, because m belongs to [u,v].
Its total use of u and v is at most t/2<=delta each; its other source
usage is no greater than before. Together with all unselected groups
it is therefore a feasible packing for w, with value f_{w'}(z)-t/2.
This proves (1). Overlap between u or v and the selected group causes
no problem: taking a set union can only reduce source usage.

By the same substitution without halving, the lower-mass compression

    w''=w-delta e_u-delta e_v+delta e_m

satisfies f_{w''}(z)<=f_w(z) at every z. Its total mass is M-delta,
so this fact alone loses delta/2^n in the desired center guarantee.

## 2. A strictly positive nonheavy example with a unique eligible pair

In Z^2 let the convex pentagon have vertices

    A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(4,2), D=(3,3), E=(0,3).

Its inequalities may be written

    x>=0, y>=0, y<=3, y>=2x-6, x+y<=6.

Thus its lattice points are the sixteen points in {0,1,2,3}^2 and the
additional point C=(4,2), exactly seventeen points. Give the five vertices
weight one, and every other lattice point weight epsilon=1/1200.
Then

    M=5+12epsilon=501/100,
    max_v w_v=1<M/4=501/400.

There are five positive-support hull vertices, more than 2^2. Their
parities are respectively 00,10,00,11,01. Consequently A,C is the
unique same-parity pair of hull vertices. Its midpoint is

    m=(2,1)=(A+C)/2=(2/3)B+(1/3)E.

## 3. Exact original maximum

At m pack the following six pair/singleton groups:

    {A,C}, {B,E}, {m}, {(1,0),(3,2)},
    {(1,1),(3,1)}, {(2,0),(2,2)}.

There are six groups: the first two have packing weight one and the
last four have packing weight epsilon. Every listed pair contains m;
all the source sets are disjoint. Hence

    f_w(m)>=2+4epsilon.

The following complete closed-halfspace table proves the reverse
global bound. For target z and normal (a,b), use

    H_z={(x,y):a(x-z_1)+b(y-z_2)>=0}.

The last two columns count the heavy vertices and other lattice points
in the cap. Direct substitution into the seventeen-point list verifies
every row.

| z | (a,b) | heavy count | other count |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| (0,0) | (-1,-1) | 1 | 0 |
| (0,1) | (-2,-1) | 1 | 1 |
| (0,2) | (-2,1) | 1 | 1 |
| (0,3) | (-1,1) | 1 | 0 |
| (1,0) | (-1,-2) | 1 | 1 |
| (1,1) | (-3,-2) | 1 | 4 |
| (1,2) | (-3,2) | 1 | 4 |
| (1,3) | (-1,2) | 1 | 1 |
| (2,0) | (1,-2) | 1 | 1 |
| (2,1) | (1,-3) | 2 | 4 |
| (2,2) | (2,3) | 2 | 4 |
| (2,3) | (1,3) | 1 | 1 |
| (3,0) | (1,-1) | 1 | 0 |
| (3,1) | (2,-3) | 1 | 2 |
| (3,2) | (2,1) | 2 | 1 |
| (3,3) | (1,2) | 1 | 0 |
| (4,2) | (1,0) | 1 | 0 |

Fractional packing is bounded above by the mass in every containing
halfspace: each containing convex-hull group must meet that halfspace.
The table therefore gives f_w(z)<=2+4epsilon for every lattice candidate.
Combined with the displayed packing,

    max_z f_w(z)=2+4epsilon=601/300.                 (2)

## 4. Every positive permitted merge strictly increases the maximum

For any 0<delta<=1, merge delta from each of A,C into 2delta at m.
At m use the same packing, now giving {A,C} weight 1-delta and the
singleton {m} weight epsilon+2delta. The pair {B,E} still has weight
one and the three small pairs still have weight epsilon. This gives

    f_{w'}(m)>=2+4epsilon+delta.

Comparison (1) and (2) give the reverse upper bound for every candidate.
Consequently

    max_z f_{w'}(z)=2+4epsilon+delta
                  =max_z f_w(z)+delta.              (3)

Thus the general additive loss in (1) is sharp even with strictly
positive original weights, no heavy source, more than 2^n hull vertices,
and only one eligible same-parity hull pair. For delta<1 the resulting
weights remain strictly positive as well. If delta=1 the zero-weight
endpoints can be deleted; the new support hull still contains m, so
the same exact maximum holds with its reduced lattice candidate set.

This disproves the desired monotonicity for every positive step size,
not merely a full endpoint deletion. It does not disprove the proposed
global inequality max_z f_w(z)>=M/2^n; the example satisfies that bound.
